title: Eating alone in New Orleans and Miami Beach
summary: He talks about his lonely meals in New Orleans and the restaurants of Miami Beach.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I don't visit those places, but I'm a lonely, I'm a lonely man, see? And I've been eating at Holmes' cafeteria because I can drive my car up in there and if I stay more than an hour, I don't have to pay any money. Otherwise, I'll have to go all over the district for a place to park and when I get in my car, somebody will hit me on the head and around me, you know? So, I don't find a food man. I can eat. I eat in the Pontchartrain too. But when they charge you a dollar and eighty cents for an armlet, that's time to stop. And not only that, they're sitting in your lap and looking down your throat and everybody... I ate breakfast there one morning, my daughter knew it at noon, your daddy was in the Pontchartrain school. Who's looking at me? But I don't care, my life is an open book. But I do walk down Weber Street because it's amusing. It's nothing but a corny island now. It's not New Orleans. It's changed, but let's have it that way. Sinister is the biggest Barnum and Bailey Shore I ever saw in my life. I go in there and walk over there. All of our boys know me. I've arranged to take a lady to breakfast in that green garden room there. They only serve meals for certain hours, you know? And then I take my daughter and when they come in, they're like, where are you going? Because they like new places. I don't blame them. If you can afford them, let's have them, huh? Like when I went to Miami and said, you want to have a room with your meals? I said, no, sir. Every meal is going to be in a different joint because Miami Beach has more fine restaurants than any place in the world. And don't they feed you? You can gain ten pounds. That stone crab. Huh? That stone crab they have there. Yeah, you bet. The first morning I go in, you see friends of mine say, don't forget to go to Wolf's Don't forget to go to Wolf's. Don't forget to go to Juniors. Don't forget to go to Lush Owls. Don't forget to go. So we go on, let's try a wall. I walk my poor wife about fifteen blocks down to Wolf's and they have a line for singles,

I mean that's the kind of business to do. I sit down and the waitress comes up and she's at the map of Israel all over her face. She's out for the money. It all hustles. Everybody hustles. So I said, honey, what do you have for breakfast? She said, you order. How about? I said, bacon and eggs, juice, and toast. She says, toast, toast as if it was poison. Where do you see what I'm going to bring here? She said, bring me a basket of every kind of bread. You can make a meal on the bread. The bread was better than the other food. Oh, you know how they do it. Stuff with dates or stuff with garlic or you never know what you're going to hit. Onion, but it's good. The place I liked was Juniors because the tables were far apart. You could go in there, you could voice.
You ever been to Juniors in Miami Beach?
And it might be two bits higher, twenty-fifths of the island, but it's worth ten dollars. You know what I mean? You're on a vacation. You're not going to come down.
